title: Equity-minded offer calibration + onboarding access log
content:
Purpose:
This doc provides a practical checklist and lightweight framework for calibrating offers with an equity lens (for historically excluded candidates, rehires, and candidates with non‑traditional backgrounds) and a companion onboarding access log to reduce first‑week friction. Use this when offers move beyond standard bands or when start logistics require special handling (delayed start, relocation stipend, visa timing, equipment exceptions).

Scope and audience:
- People Ops partners and Recruiting Leads
- Hiring managers and Compensation approvers
- Security/IT onboarding engineers
- Solutions/ESG partners for special accommodation approvals

High-level principles (short):
1) Transparency: Document rationale for adjustments and assumptions (market data, internal parity). Keep notes attached to offer packet.
2) Equity-first adjustments: Consider non-salary compensation (sign-on, stipend, flexible schedule, learning budget) where salary parity would cause internal compression.
3) Reduce friction: Pre-stage accesses and equipment where possible to create a warm first week.
4) Risk-bounded flexibility: Small ad-hoc sweeteners OK with hiring manager signoff; larger deviations require Compensation review and Director approval.

Offer calibration flow (quick steps):
- Hiring manager submits proposed level + base + equity % + sign-on + relocation stipend (if any) into offer template (recruiting-offer-template).
- People Ops runs internal parity check: compare to two closest peers (same level, similar tenure) and document rationale.
- If candidate is from historically excluded background, add a note describing barriers we are compensating for (e.g., undocumented contract history, non-traditional remit).
- Consider non-financial accelerators (accelerated review for promotion bump, mentorship credit, learning stipend).
- Compensation team decision within 48 hours for deviations <= 15% of band; >15% escalates to Director/Finance.
- Finalize packet and send to candidate with transparent explanation of total comp (base, equity, sign-ons, perks).

Offer adjustment heuristics (examples):
- Market catch-up: If market data shows candidate requires +10–20% relative to midpoint, prefer sign-on + faster review cycle vs permanent compression.
- Rejoiners: keep total comp continuity; offer retention sign-on only if gap > 10% vs last Redwood comp.
- International hires: factor visa timing uncertainty into start-date flexibility and pro-rate sign-ons where applicable.

Hiring manager checklist (before send):
- [ ] Documented leveling rationale + 2 peer comparators
- [ ] Proposed comp and any ad-hoc items listed with reasons
- [ ] Manager sign‑off (name + date)
- [ ] People Ops parity note inserted
- [ ] Compensation approval (if required)

Equity-minded considerations (non-standard but recommended):
- Relocation alternatives (remote onboarding stipend, co-working reimbursements)
- Upfront desk/ergonomic budget if candidate has constraints
- Immediate mentorship credit: guarantee of 6‑12 months of mentoring hours and reviewer bandwidth for promotion within 12 months
- Partial sign‑on in milestone schedule (e.g., 50% at start, 50% at 6 months) to support retention while managing cash flow

Onboarding access log (use this to track gating items; fill dates and owner):
- Preboard: offer accepted -> People Ops creates starter packet + legal -> assign buddy
- IT: laptop order placed (date), asset tag, expected delivery date, temporary loaner assigned? (Y/N)
- Accounts: email created (date), SSO enabled (date), VPN/MFA enrollment (date)
- Codebase: read-only repo access (date), environment sandbox credentials (date)
- Infra: cloud account creation (date), minimal compute quota assigned (date)
- Product: feature backlog read; assigned intro tickets (date)
- Security training: assigned modules (date assigned / date completed)
- Manager: 1:1 schedule for first 30 days created (date)
- Mentor: mentor assigned + intro meeting scheduled (date)
- Compliance: required background/visa docs received (date)

(Onboarding access log template row format — copy into recruiting Slack thread):
"Candidate name | Start date | Laptop ordered (date) | Email | SSO | VPN | Repo access | Mentor | First-PR-assigned | Notes"

Priority preboarding tasks (first 7 days):
1) Welcome note + org map (send day 0)
2) Launcher checklist sent with first-week schedule (day 0)
3) Equip delivery confirmation (day -1 or day 1)
4) Buddy intro + 1:1 scheduled (day 1)
5) Minimal contributor path: tiny ticket to merge on day 3–5

Micro-access concept (reduce cognitive load):
- Start with least-privilege read-only access to 2–3 repos + staging environment for experiments. Grant write/exec privileges after a successful security checklist and manager sign-off (typically 2–4 weeks). Document date and rationale in the access log.

Interview rubric summary (compact; to include with offer evidence):
Competencies (score 1–5 each):
- Problem-solving: clarity of approach, tradeoff reasoning, debugging craft (1 = poor, 5 = exemplary).
- System design or product sense: appropriate for role (scale, latency, user impact).
- Collaboration & communication: cross-team clarity, stakeholder sensitivity.
- Ownership & delivery: ability to scope, deliver, and follow up.
- Growth potential & learning agility: evidence of learning from feedback and ramp speed.
Decision rule: candidate passes bar if average >= 3.5 and no competency below 2. Tie-breaker: manager + interview panel discuss, consider domain-specific signals and references.

Documentation to attach to offer packet (minimal):
- Interview rubric scores (CSV or screenshot)
- Peer parity note (1 paragraph)
- Any special accommodations agreed (start flexibility, stipend, visa notes)

Case studies (short examples):
1) Non-traditional engineer with 5 yrs contracting + portfolio: used learning stipend + small sign-on, assigned mentor and clear 6-month promotion check. Result: accepted and promotion within 8 months.
2) Candidate with constrained relocation window: offered remote onboarding stipend + co-working credit and pro-rated relocation; started remote, relocated at 3 months.

Escalation path for unusual requests:
- Manager -> People Ops -> Compensation -> Director -> Finance (use this ordering; add Slack thread link and approval snapshot).

Open questions / follow-ups for central HR team:
- Standardize approach for milestone sign-ons (legal & payroll constraints across regions).
- Should we formalize micro-access expiry policy (recommended 90 days default)?
- Create template language for explaining equity/grant calculations to candidates in plain English.

How to use this doc in practice (one‑pager):
- For any non-standard offer, run through the quick heuristics above and populate the onboarding access log at offer acceptance. Save a copy of the filled access log to the candidate folder in Drive and tag the hiring manager.

Appendix: sample intro paragraph for offer email (transparent and equity-minded):
"We’re excited to extend an offer for the role of Senior Software Engineer. The package below reflects our commitment to fair and transparent offers: your base, equity grant, and a sign-on that helps address any market or hiring transition gaps. We’ve documented how we arrived at this packet; if any part of this needs clarification or a different structure to support your start, we’re happy to discuss."

Notes and links:
- Reference paybands doc: hr-paybands-v4.xlsx
- Related Confluence: CONFLUENCE-3142 (equity comp principles)
- Recruiting template: recruiting-offer-template (internal)
